Industry News: Tested: 2027 Subaru Forester Wilderness Hybrid Is a Fuel-Economy-Hero Of a Soft-Roader

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1017 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Roadandtrack

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, decades before the advent of the soft-roader, Subaru was building everyday cars with a limited amount of extra off-road capability.
  • Naturally, Subaru has now combined the two by offering a Forester Hybrid in Wilderness trim.
  • Sources indicate that our expert editors test every vehicle we review.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, decades before the advent of the soft-roader, Subaru was building everyday cars with a limited amount of extra off-road capability. So it should be no surprise that its Wilderness line of slightly more capable crossovers has been a hit. So, too, has Subaru’s integration of hybrid systems, in an era when buyers of volume cars such as the Forester are happy to get their hands on anything that means greater efficiency.

Naturally, Subaru has now combined the two by offering a Forester Hybrid in Wilderness trim. The recipe seems like a sales hit waiting to happen, but is it worth the extra complexity?

Sources indicate that our expert editors test every vehicle we review. Read more about how we test and review cars here.

Subaru finally brought a hybrid powertrain to the Forester for the 2025 model year. A newly introduced Wilderness was introduced a few months later, but it lacked the gas-electric system available on the basic car. The Forester Wilderness Hybrid combines the two, allowing Subaru to offer a system peak of 194 horsepower from a 2.5-liter flat-four and a 1-kWh battery pack.

Sources indicate that EPA-estimated fuel economy is down slightly from the basic Forester Hybrid, but the 33 mpg city and 29 mpg highway are still both solid numbers for a crossover with 9.3 inches of ground clearance and Yokohama Geolander all-terrain tires. For most buyers, that improvement alone should justify the price, which is $1000 more than the basic Forester Wilderness.

Powertrain: 2.5-liter Atkinson-cycle flat-four, lithium-ion hydride battery pack.

Power: 194 hp @ 5600 rpm (peak system output).

Transmission: continuously variable automatic, all-wheel drive.

EPA mpg: 33 city, 29 highway, 31 combined.

Befitting the Wilderness Hybrid’s soft-roader credentials, the media drive took place on the dirt, grass, and gravel roads of a private ranch. While this made for beautiful scenery, it did little to showcase what the car could do as a daily driver or challenge its off-road capabilities.

According to recent reports, those capabilities did impress on a more technical off-roading course that Subaru built for the event, although that comes with the caveat that the company presumably built the course with the car’s limits in mind. Even though this is ultimately still a relatively conventional crossover with nothing like the articulation of a more extreme off-roader, the all-terrain tires were capable of handling substantial ruts and steep hill descents.

Recent findings suggest that approach, break-over, and departure angles of 23.5, 20.6, and 25.5 degrees, respectively, are identical to the nonhybrid Forester Wilderness. This hybrid crossover has the clearance to get over obstacles a car camper or kayaker might find on the trail to their favorite outdoor-recreation spot. The biggest frustration here was the low resolution of the X-Drive off-road menus built into the infotainment screens, a feature that felt behind the respectable capabilities of the crossover itself.

Sources indicate that while the off-road performance is what sets the Wilderness apart from its more pedestrian Forester Hybrid brethren, limited on-road testing suggests that the car feels similar in everyday situations. Given the all-terrain tires, that’s a solid achievement, even if the end result is still relative mediocrity. This Forester is no performance car, and anyone who might have been expecting a canyon carver will instead have to make do with relaxed acceleration and a frustrating continuously variable automatic transmission.

The Forester is a tentpole for Subaru because it combines the basic compact-crossover shape today’s buyers want with some degree of utility in all forms. The Wilderness goes one step further in providing even more capability, but its day-to-day strength will be how little it sacrifices to do that.

Sources indicate that the Forester Wilderness Hybrid drops 5 mpg of efficiency in the city in comparison to the standard Forester Hybrid, for 33 mpg. The basic Forester Wilderness, by contrast, gets just 24 mpg in the city. The hybrid remains relatively comfortable and quiet on the road too, which is great news for buyers who do not want to hear harsh noises from all-terrain tires and the unique drone of a Subaru boxer engine all day.

Still, the Wilderness line is differentiated by its capabilities. Buyers looking for a soft-roader do expect to use the car on a trail every so often, which makes the Wilderness Hybrid’s lack of a spare tire a major issue. Since components of the hybrid system are packed where a spare would go on a normal Wilderness, buyers of this car will either have to find another way to carry a fifth tire or contend with the reality that a flat could derail their outdoor adventures in a worse way than the same problem would in the nonhybrid model.

That missing spare tire is one of two major drawbacks for the Wilderness Hybrid. The other is the towing capacity, down from 3500 pounds to just 1500. Both of these are serious limitations for buyers who have certain use cases in mind for their soft-roader, but neither is necessarily a problem for the average buyer. The price difference is not negligible, but fuel savings should cover the difference in cost within a few years. For most buyers, that makes the Hybrid the obvious choice.

Recent findings suggest that buyers looking at other hybrid soft-roaders could also consider the new Toyota RAV4 Woodland and the Honda CR-V Trailsport. The Subaru is the only one of the three hybrids with conventional full-time all-wheel drive, although that specific differentiator is not necessarily a game changer for buyers who will be spending most of their time on the street. For those who do need to venture a little further a little more often, though, the Forester Hybrid Wilderness seems like the strongest choice.

Subaru’s Wilderness models are sold with synthetic StarTex interiors meant to be easily cleaned, and this particular vehicle even includes a synthetic steering-wheel cover in lieu of the usual leather. This is a small detail for most, but it does mean that the cabin is entirely vegan. For some very specific buyers, however, that one detail could make all the difference.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Amflow has made a name for itself in the electric mountain bike world with its high-performance Avinox-powered machines, but now the company is bringing that same technology to a decidedly more urban environment.
  • And while these might look like fairly conventional step-through city bikes at first glance, there’s some seriously impressive technology hiding beneath those clean lines.
  • The fresh Amflow UE series comes in two versions, the UE Carbon and the higher-end UE Carbon Pro, both built around a full-carbon fiber frame weighing just 2.35 kg (5.2 lb).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Amflow has made a name for itself in the electric mountain bike world with its high-performance Avinox-powered machines, but now the company is bringing that same technology to a decidedly more urban environment. The newly unveiled Amflow UE Carbon series marks the brand’s first move into the commuter e-bike market, combining a lightweight carbon fiber frame, powerful mid-drive motor, and a surprisingly long list of smart features designed for everyday riding.

And while these might look like fairly conventional step-through city bikes at first glance, there’s some seriously impressive technology hiding beneath those clean lines.

The fresh Amflow UE series comes in two versions, the UE Carbon and the higher-end UE Carbon Pro, both built around a full-carbon fiber frame weighing just 2.35 kg (5.2 lb).

The complete bike weighs as little as 20.9 kg (46 lb), which is fairly impressive considering the amount of hardware Amflow has packed into it, including front suspension, a suspension dropper seatpost, integrated lighting, and cargo racks.

According to recent reports, both models use the Avinox M2 mid-drive motor, which delivers up to 125 Nm of torque. That’s an enormous amount of torque for a city bike, and should make short work of steep hills, especially when carrying groceries or other cargo. And to put things into perspective, a lot of city e-bikes have barely 60 Nm for torque, so Amflow is knocking it out of the park for urban power.

A removable 600 Wh battery provides a claimed maximum range of 132 km (82 miles) in the lowest power assist mode, while fast charging can refill the battery in just 2 hours and 23 minutes.

The bikes also feature Avinox’s intelligent traction control system and a new Auto Boost function that automatically provides additional assistance when the system detects demanding conditions, such as accelerating from a stop or climbing a steep hill.

In other words, riders get much of the sophisticated motor technology developed for high-performance electric mountain bikes, but in a package designed for commuting to work or picking up groceries.

Recent findings suggest that the bike is listed as weighing 20.9 kg (46 lb), though that figure conveniently excludes the front and rear racks, mudguards, pedals, kickstand, bike lock, bottle cage, and chainguard. So figure a few extra pounds for all of that gear, and you’re in the right ballpark.

The main difference between the two models is their drivetrain.

The higher-end UE Carbon Pro ($3,899) uses a customized three-speed electronically shifted internally geared hub paired with a Gates carbon belt drive. That should make it particularly appealing to commuters who want a quiet, clean, low-maintenance setup without worrying about chain lubrication or derailleur adjustments.

The more affordable UE Carbon ($3,499) instead uses a 10-speed electronic derailleur developed with TRP.

Both models support automatic shifting, allowing the bike to handle gear changes without requiring the rider to constantly think about them.

Amflow has also gone fairly wild with the technology integration.

There’s a 1.4-inch touchscreen display mounted on the handlebars, a wireless phone charging mount offering 15W wireless charging or 20W USB-C charging, and integrated lighting with automatic low-light activation and brake-sensing functionality.

The bikes even include a hardened steel frame lock on the rear wheel, Apple Find My integration, and a Lost Mode feature that can lock down certain components if the bike is stolen.

Apple Watch connectivity allows riders to check their bike’s status and unlock it, while heart-rate-based assistance can automatically adjust motor output to help riders maintain a target heart rate zone.

Some of these features, like the security and tracking, are immediately effective for nearly all riders, while other high-tech features like the heart rate-based pedal assist can provide even more functionality for niche riders looking to bridge the gap between riding for transportation and riding for fitness.

Of course, all the fancy technology in the world doesn’t mean much if a commuter bike can’t handle everyday errands.

Fortunately, Amflow appears to have taken the practical side seriously.

The bikes feature a low step-through frame, upright riding position, 65 mm suspension fork, and a suspension dropper seatpost offering 125 mm of height adjustment and approximately 30 mm of suspension travel.

The 26×2.0-inch Maxxis tires should also provide a comfortable ride over less-than-perfect city streets.

There’s a front rack rated for 20 kg (44 lb) and a rear rack rated for 27 kg (59.5 lb), with the latter supporting the MIK HD mounting system for compatible accessories, including child seats.

The standard frame is designed to accommodate riders from 155 to 190 cm (5’1” to 6’3”), while a smaller version for riders down to 140 cm (4’7”) is expected in 2027.

I’ve been impressed with the technology coming out of the Avinox ecosystem, and it’s exciting to see that technology finally make its way into a more practical city-focused electric bicycle.

Recent findings suggest that as much as I love high-performance electric mountain bikes, the reality is that most people aren’t spending their mornings bombing down mountain trails. They’re commuting to work, dropping kids off at school, and running errands.

And that’s where electric bicycles can make an even bigger difference.

In a recent development, the Amflow UE series seems to take a refreshingly comprehensive approach to urban riding. The powerful motor is nice, but I’m arguably more interested in the belt drive, integrated security, cargo capacity, automatic shifting, and built-in phone charging.

Those are the kinds of features that can make an electric bicycle genuinely easier to live with every day. And as someone who actually commutes with an e-bike each day as my main form of transportation, these bikes are really speaking to me!

If you ask me, it’s great to see another high-performance e-bike manufacturer recognizing that the future of electric bicycles isn’t just about riding farther and faster on trails. It’s also about making everyday transportation better for the less exciting type of riding, too.

If you can believe it, Love and Deepspace is almost two-years-old, and Infold Games is celebrating the moment in a few major ways. The Throne of Eros upgrade brings the game up to version 5.0, and it’s one for fans of all love interests.

Recent findings suggest that for one, this is the first time all five of them are brought together. The upgrade is also adding some important new features, alongside anniversary events, and more.

Throne of Eros also doubles as the new Wish Pool, which is the one that has all of the game’s love interests in a single banner. This is a limited-time affair, of course, but it’s not the only thing you should look forward to here.

There’s also the Memory Growth Bonus, another limited-time event that you can take advantage of to grow your Memories. The even bigger news is that you can target your Wishes through the Xspace Echo, which lets you select five Memories to create your own pool from. You can use this to get any Memories you might not have, of course.

On the topic of Memories, you’ll also be able to unlock latest second anniversary KV Memories, as part of a Yearly Highlights Event that will let you look back on your own journey with the game over the past year.

On the story and narrative side, Throne of Eros adds two new main stories, with new branches for Xavier, and Rafayel. There’s even a narrative-specific event that will run throughout the anniversary period, through which you can earn two daily outfits for each of the five love interests.

Sources indicate that the celebrations also extend to newly introduced anniversary content like mail, and video calls. You can purchase a Yearly Pass, and check out some new arrivals at the Lunar Shop.

Beyond the anniversary content, version 5.0 also adds a latest feature to the game: Home, which essentially offers a hub to get you directly to interacting with love interests that doesn’t have to do with combat or story.

You can also expect various other quality of life updates that touch on the Journal, Phone Moments Search, Resources Quick Cleanup, and latest Tete-a-Tete that should make interacting with all of them more streamlined.

It has been revealed that while this is a special banner, you should brush up on how banners work in Love and Deepspace if you’re unfamiliar. As always, it’s never not a good idea to check our Love and Deepspace codes page for some freebies.

FDA Initiates Labeling Changes for GLP-1s Due to Rare But Serious Eye Disease Risk

💡 Key Takeaways
  • GLP-1 customers have a new symptom to watch for: Sudden vision loss in one eye.
  • In a recent development, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) declared on November 9 that it will require drugmakers to add information to the warning labels of Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Zepbound and other GLP-1 medications about “a potential increased risk” of a rare eye condition called nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION).GLP-1 medications are approved to treat type 2 diabetes and to help people lose weight and keep it off.NAION joins a growing list of side effects linked to GLP-1s, adding a second eye warning to several labels.The U.S.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GLP-1 customers have a new symptom to watch for: Sudden vision loss in one eye.

In a recent development, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) declared on November 9 that it will require drugmakers to add information to the warning labels of Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Zepbound and other GLP-1 medications about “a potential increased risk” of a rare eye condition called nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION).GLP-1 medications are approved to treat type 2 diabetes and to help people lose weight and keep it off.NAION joins a growing list of side effects linked to GLP-1s, adding a second eye warning to several labels.The U.S. labels for Ozempic, Rybelsus, Trulicity, Mounjaro, and Zepbound already warn about diabetic retinopathy, a diabetes-related eye disease, according to each drug’s prescribing information.The two conditions affect different parts of the eye. Diabetic retinopathy damages tiny blood vessels in the retina, the layer at the back of the eye that senses light, according to the National Eye Institute. NAION damages the optic nerve when it doesn’t get enough blood, according to the FDA’s announcement.Mihail Zilbermint, MD, director of endocrine hospitalists at Johns Hopkins, told Healthline he hasn’t seen NAION in his patients. He has seen vision worsen in some people after they start a GLP-1.“But we believe that’s probably related to rapid improvement in their sugar control, which can also be seen in someone who is starting insulin,” Zilbermint mentioned.

A 2024 study published in JAMA Ophthalmology “initially triggered” the FDA’s review, the agency told Healthline.

Recent findings suggest that the study found a higher risk of NAION in people prescribed semaglutide, the active ingredient in Ozempic and Wegovy, than in people prescribed other diabetes or weight-loss drugs.The authors wrote that more research is needed to determine whether semaglutide causes NAION.Joseph F. Rizzo III, MD, director of the Neuro-Ophthalmology Service at Mass Eye and Ear in Boston, served as the study’s corresponding author.

Recent findings suggest that in a 2024 podcast, Rizzo noted he and a resident saw three patients with NAION who were taking semaglutide for about a week.“And because NAION is a fairly uncommon disorder in the general population, the fact that we had three within a relatively short period of time led me to suspect that there was a higher risk of developing NAION in patients on semaglutide,” Rizzo said. The FDA analyzed clinical trials for multiple GLP-1 drugs and noted that NAION cases were reported with every GLP-1 on the market, according to its announcement. Those findings led the FDA to require the warning for the entire drug class, the agency told Healthline.

About 70% to 80% of people with NAION first notice vision loss when they wake up, according to StatPearls. The FDA listed these symptoms:.

No treatment has been proven to reverse vision loss from NAION, according to StatPearls.

“Patients experiencing sudden, painless vision loss in one eye should contact their healthcare professional immediately and should not stop their medication without consulting their provider first,” the FDA told Healthline.

In the announcement, the agency told doctors to promptly refer patients with suspected NAION to an ophthalmologist.

The FDA listed these possible risk factors for NAION:.

The FDA told Healthline that many people who take GLP-1s also have these conditions, which made reports of NAION in GLP-1 users “challenging” to interpret.

In a recent development, across 126 clinical trials, the FDA found about 6 NAION cases per 100,000 people taking a GLP-1 for a year, and about 4 per 100,000 people taking a placebo or another diabetes drug for a year.In real-world data, NAION was more common with GLP-1s than with one type of diabetes pill, but the FDA found no significant increase compared with another type, the agency told Healthline.Zilbermint said patients who saw the news have worried about losing their vision. He tells them that “many of the serious harms, including the potential harm of NAION, are rare.”“The overall risk is still very small,” he said.

Regulators in other countries have added NAION warnings, mostly for semaglutide:.

The FDA told Healthline the benefits of GLP-1s “continue to outweigh their risks when used as directed.”The FDA has also approved some GLP-1s to lower the risk of heart attack and stroke, reduce the risk of worsening kidney disease, and treat sleep apnea and a type of liver disease.Zilbermint said that “for most of my patients with obesity, diabetes and heart disease, the benefits clearly outweigh the risks.”“But we definitely have to decide patient by patient,” he added.

The labeling change applies to these medications, according to the FDA’s announcement:.

Taking a vintage muscle car and swapping in modern components to make it run better or add power is a story as old as, well, the LS2 V-8. Vintage Modern’s newly introduced Fastback Mustang turns that formula upside down—by swapping old-school body parts onto a modern S650-generation Mustang GT. But the Vintage Modern Fastback, officially revealed on Wednesday at Retromobile New York, is more than just a body kit.

Other high-end Mustang features like active-valve performance exhaust with four sound modes, MagneRide adaptive suspension, six selectable drive modes, and Brembo performance brakes are also standard fare.

Sources indicate that even though the bones of the Fastback are from a current-generation Mustang, the heavily modified vehicle still underwent crash testing to meet applicable Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards. This retro-inspired Mustang features eight airbags, crumple zones, side-impact beams, electronic stability control, traction control, and anti-lock brakes. That’s more than most restomod Mustang owners can say.

Sources indicate that most of the custom body panels, including the functional hood scoop, are carbon fiber; the only obviously metal pieces are the billet-aluminum grille, door handles, mirrors, and twin auxiliary driving lights. Similarly, the interior of the retro Fastback build features Alcantara and billet-aluminum trim over three different seat upholsteries: pleated, diamond-quilted, or woven. Each buyer can choose from more than 40 standard paint colors, as well as paint-to-sample finishes and stripe options, along with their own interior configurations; Vintage Modern is also offering an optional JL Audio premium sound system and leather-trimmed floor mats.

In a recent development, vintage Modern’s carbon-fiber body panels are hand-made in Detroit before being assembled and finished at its Atlanta facility; all told, each unit requires around 900 hours of hands-on labor. The builder has significant plans, too; it claims it has plans to move into a fresh factory three times the size of its existing facility, hire more than 100 additional team members, and triple production capacity within two years.

No pricing details about the Vintage Modern Fastback were available at the time of publication, but we’ll revision this story when we learn more.

Ford has entered the battery business. The first LFP battery cells are now rolling off the assembly line at Ford’s BlueOval Battery Park plant in Michigan and are headed to power Fathom prototypes in Kentucky.

Industry observers note that how do you get more out of a battery without adding weight or more cells? According to Alan Clarke, Ford’s vice president of advanced development projects, who is also leading its Universal Electric Vehicle (UEV) platform, the answer lies in lithium iron phosphate (LFP) technology.

Industry observers note that unlike traditional lithium-ion, LFP batteries use no nickel or cobalt, which helps reduce costs. They also typically hold up better after years of use and charging.

According to recent reports, to make it a reality, Ford turned to CATL, the leading global EV battery manufacturer. Ford uses CATL’s licensed technology and manufacturing expertise at its BlueOval Battery Park Michigan plant.

Ford remarked it will be the first in the US to deliver LFP batteries for mainstream automotive use, with the battery cells now rolling off the line in Michigan.

The first LFP battery cells are headed to Ford’s Louisville Assembly Plant and will be used to power Fathom prototypes, its first vehicle based on the UEV platform.

Sources indicate that ford designed and engineered the Fathom from the ground up for efficiency. As such, it chose prismatic battery cells because they fit directly into the chassis, reducing structural costs.

With cells now being delivered from a plant that it owns and operates, Ford remarked it will use the knowledge gained in Michigan to support more affordable EVs and Ford Energy, its fresh battery energy storage business in Kentucky.

At Ford’s newly introduced battery plant in Michigan, assembly lines can deliver 40 cells every minute, making it one of the fastest LFP prismatic battery assembly lines outside China.

Although the accelerated output drives down costs, Ford said employees use AI-powered image recognition and inspection tools to spot defects in real time and maintain quality.

“Our goal is to make defective cells so rare that we track their frequency per billion cells rather than per million,” Ford mentioned.

With production testing now underway, Ford aims to have the battery pack plant in Michigan up and running in 2027, ahead of schedule.

Ford will open preorders for the Fathom in early 2027, starting at $28,350 for the standard-range model.

CEO Jim Farley said on the company’s third-quarter earnings call last month that the Fathom, Ford’s first vehicle based on the UEV platform, remains on track to launch in Q4 2027.

Farley said the Fathom is a “breakthrough product” that’s highly capable and still affordable. The starting MSRP is under $30,000, and the low cost of ownership is perfect for today’s market, he added.

Recent findings suggest that ford and Slate both producing vehicles with US-produced LFP batteries is a great milestone. Hopefully we can keep pushing our domestic battery supply chain forward.

Ford noted the Fathom will offer more interior space than a Toyota RAV4, and it will cost less to own over five years than a three-year-old used Tesla Model Y.

The pickup will be the first vehicle to integrate Apple Maps directly into the navigation system. All versions will be BlueCruise-capable for hands-free driving, with standard Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, plus bidirectional charging capabilities.

Although we have yet to see it, Ford stated the Fathom features a “large touchscreen display” with easy-to-use navigation.

Ford has not revealed battery specs or range, but we do know the pickup will have an NACS port after several prototypes were spotted at a Tesla Supercharger over the summer.

Democracy Depends on Being Able to Forgive

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (899 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 19, 2026 | Reviewed by Jessica Schrader.
  • Industry observers note that in a 60 Minutes interview broadcast this month, President Trump was asked a profound question that rarely comes up in political interviews: Could he forgive his enemies?
  • It has been revealed that “The answer is no,” the president noted.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 19, 2026 | Reviewed by Jessica Schrader.

Industry observers note that in a 60 Minutes interview broadcast this month, President Trump was asked a profound question that rarely comes up in political interviews: Could he forgive his enemies? If entering heaven required him to feel love and forgiveness for James Comey or Nancy Pelosi, could he do it?

It has been revealed that “The answer is no,” the president noted. “I want to be honest, no.”.

In a recent development, we should resist the tempting thought that only Donald Trump feels this way. We all instead need to look in the mirror: How willing are we to forgive the people we believe have done us wrong?

For most of us, grievance has a powerful pull—whether it’s rehearsing an argument or replaying a hurtful remark over and over in our heads. In psychology, we can understand forgiveness as a voluntary change in how we feel and act toward someone who’s hurt us in the past. It can loosen the hold of resentment on our attention and, in turn, help us choose how to respond in the future.

It has been revealed that these days, the word forgiveness can sound like a concept out of a Sunday school class or a therapy session. But it’s a prerequisite for a functioning democratic society.

In a recent development, A country needs ways to respond to wrongdoing and still leave open the possibility of a shared future. When every injury becomes a reason for retaliation, the work of governing turns into settling scores.

Recent findings suggest that here’s the thing about democracy: It’s a continuing relationship among fallible people. It depends on our ability to correct errors, acknowledge wrongdoing, and work together again. Forgiveness is a vital civic skill because democratic societies have to do more than settle who was right in the last conflict. Forgiveness makes healthy debate and cooperation possible.

In a recent development, I once asked the legendary Archbishop Desmond Tutu what forgiveness meant. He simply said, “It means I no longer demand payback from you.”.

When he was chair of South Africa’s Truth and Reconciliation Commission, Tutu helped bring apartheid-era abuses to public attention. He underscored the principle that forgiveness isn’t blanket absolution. Truth, accountability, and repair can coexist with refusing permanent vengeance. In our own lives, we can forgive someone while maintaining boundaries, including choosing not to resume a relationship.

In a recent development, when I interviewed former Colombian president and Nobel Peace laureate Juan Manuel Santos for my book On Belonging, he recalled advice to recognise an adversary’s humanity in war and peace. His 2016 agreement with the FARC opened a path for former guerrillas to enter into democratic politics.

This month, delivering the Nelson Mandela Annual Lecture in South Africa, Santos told the story of Pastora Mira. She cared for a wounded man who then confessed to torturing and killing her son. She embraced him, saying his acceptance of responsibility had freed her from the prison of lifelong hatred. It’s a breathtaking example. Such forgiveness remains a personal choice.

In a recent development, it’s key that we avoid thinking that the psychological grip of contempt is unique to any one country. Others—including my home country of Canada—shouldn’t think they’re immune to a politics of contempt. A 2025 Angus Reid Institute–Cardus survey found 87% of Conservative supporters regarded the Liberals as a threat to Canada’s well-being. And 84% of Liberal supporters stated the same of Conservatives.

According to recent reports, the philosopher Hannah Arendt understood forgiveness as a way to release people from being bound indefinitely to what they’ve done, allowing something upcoming to begin. For her, forgiveness was inextricably linked to respect and to what I call belonging—that we honour people’s humanity, even if we disagree with their preferences.

Earlier this month, Texans elected James Talarico, a Presbyterian seminarian, to the U.S. Senate. He’s spoken eloquently about loving his enemies and seeing opponents as children of God. It’s a message that draws on a Christian tradition that asks us to extend the mercy we ourselves need—a tradition Martin Luther King Jr. brought into public life more than half a century ago.

According to recent reports, ultimately, forgiveness is a skill we can learn. In an international study of more than 4,500 adults, people given a short program to reflect on hurt and consider another person’s perspective reported greater forgiveness and fewer symptoms of depression and anxiety after two weeks than those waiting to begin. The study concerned personal relationships, but it offers reason to take forgiveness seriously as something we can actively cultivate.

We can all put this into practice. Name what happened and how it honestly affected your feelings. Try to consider the other person’s perspective, and think of a time you needed forgiveness for yourself. Give yourself time and space for your feelings to change. Choosing to forgive can precede feeling the emotion of forgiveness.

Industry observers note that let’s face it: In failing to forgive his enemies, Donald Trump isn’t so much of an outlier. But that needs to change. To build a healthy democratic society, we can’t have permanent enemies. We have to build a future together. That work can begin in our own relationships.

Breaking: Potatoes grown in moon dirt are as nutritious as Earth potatoes

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (578 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Astronauts living in the first permanent lunar base may see a sizable number of spuds on their dinner plates.
  • “We found that potatoes can complete their entire life cycle in simulated lunar soil when supplemented with organic matter,” Aymeric Goyer, an OSU botanist and study co-author, mentioned in a statement.
  • According to recent reports, even in a controlled habitat, life on the moon will be physically demanding for astronauts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Astronauts living in the first permanent lunar base may see a sizable number of spuds on their dinner plates. In a study published today in the journal npj Microgravity, botanists at Oregon State University (OSU) proved it’s possible to grow healthy, edible potatoes in simulated moon soil with the help of everyday worms. Importantly, the team also identified the proper proportions of lunar regolith and compost needed to produce potato yields similar to those grown on Earth.

“We found that potatoes can complete their entire life cycle in simulated lunar soil when supplemented with organic matter,” Aymeric Goyer, an OSU botanist and study co-author, mentioned in a statement. “That’s an vital step toward developing reliable food production systems that could support long-term human exploration of the Moon.”.

According to recent reports, even in a controlled habitat, life on the moon will be physically demanding for astronauts. They’ll require carefully maintained, nutritious diets to keep them healthy, but it’s not as simple as sending them off packed with calorically dense prepackaged meals. Cargo room on spacecraft is limited and costly, and the desolate lunar surface isn’t exactly hospitable to agriculture. In addition to constant bombardment by cosmic and solar radiation, temperatures can swing anywhere between 250 degrees and -410 degrees Fahrenheit.

Industry observers note that indoor horticulture will also be challenging. Lunar regolith is an annoyingly powdery substance composed of sharp-edged, miniscule particles created over billions of years of asteroid impacts, but little else. With essentially no organic material at all, the dust alone isn’t capable of supporting plant life.

It has been revealed that while it is easy enough to combine that lunar regolith with agricultural additives, researchers weren’t sure if these could overcome moon soil’s heavy metals and irradiation. To test it, Goyer and his colleagues first obtained simulated lunar regolith made to resemble the samples collected during the Apollo missions. Regolith composition varies by region on the moon, so they selected five different types based on darker lunar mare dust and the lighter lunar highland soil. They then mixed the mock moon dust with vermicompost, the nutrient-rich soil created when worms break down organic materials. Next, they planted potatoes in various ratios of regolith and vermicompost, and monitored their growth. As a control, the team even planted potatoes in soil taken from Hermiston, Oregon, an area famous for some of the world’s highest spud yields.

According to recent reports, the team found that composite soil with only 30 percent vermicompost was enough to produce potato crops comparable to those farmed on Earth. Their findings suggest the supplemental organics bind to the regolith’s heavy metals, which shield the plants and minimize any damage to their roots.

“We believe the compost helps balance some of the toxicity we see in lunar regolith,” added OSU botanist and study co-author David Handy.

In a recent development, but bushels of moon potatoes only go so far if they lack any real nutritional value. Even here, the lunar simulations offered promising results, particularly when it came to glycoalkaloids. The naturally forming potato toxins can cause green skin discoloration, but analysis indicated no statistically relevant rise in glycoalkaloids for the lunar crops.

With the potato viability debate settled, Goyer’s team will next compare 10 specific spud varieties grown in simulated lunar regolith to determine the most nutritious and resilient options for NASA astronomers.

1 in 3 Infants Diagnosed With Peanut Allergy May Not Have the Condition

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (921 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Peanut allergies have been on the rise in recent decades.
  • According to statistics provided by Food Allergy Research & Education (FARE), an estimated 6.2 million children and adults in the United States are allergic to peanuts.
  • However, newly introduced research published in the November 2026 matter of The Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology suggests that over a third of infants thought to have this diagnosis might not actually have a peanut allergy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Peanut allergies have been on the rise in recent decades.

According to statistics provided by Food Allergy Research & Education (FARE), an estimated 6.2 million children and adults in the United States are allergic to peanuts.

However, newly introduced research published in the November 2026 matter of The Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology suggests that over a third of infants thought to have this diagnosis might not actually have a peanut allergy.

In fact, having a history of reacting to peanuts and positive allergy testing on their own may not be sufficient to diagnose a peanut allergy for many infants.

The study’s authors suggest that a threshold oral food challenge — in which the child is given increasing amounts of the suspected food allergen under medical supervision to look for an allergic reaction — should be routinely considered to help confirm peanut allergy.

This additional testing could safely prevent children who are not allergic to peanuts from undergoing unnecessary treatment with oral immunotherapy.

It could also spare families from burdensome food restrictions and allergy precautions.

The researchers’ goal was to evaluate the accuracy and safety of the Allergy Development to an Accelerated Path to Tolerance (ADAPT) peanut oral immunotherapy program, which was established in 2024 at 10 public children’s hospitals across Australia.

This program provides a standardized approach to evaluating and treating infants with suspected peanut allergies.

The study included infants who had experienced a mild to moderate reaction to peanut before 12 months of age and had evidence of peanut sensitization through allergy testing.

Researchers reviewed medical records to examine how accurately the program’s approach identified peanut allergies and whether it could safely guide treatment.

Industry observers note that A key part of the evaluation was a threshold oral food challenge. The challenge involved up to seven doses, ranging from 15 to 1,300 milligrams of peanut protein.

Medical teams monitored the infants for reactions and provided treatment when necessary.

Researchers reviewed records from April 2024 through October 2025. During that period, 1,275 infants were assessed through the program, and 778 underwent an oral food challenge.

The researchers also examined allergy test results and whether infants who reacted during the challenges could begin oral immunotherapy at an appropriate starting dose.

At the time of the oral food challenge, the infants had a median age of 13 months.

Of the 778 infants who underwent an oral food challenge, 507 (65.2%) had an allergic reaction.

However, 271 (34.8%) did not react to peanut during the supervised test, despite having a history of a previous reaction and positive allergy test results.

These findings suggest that relying on medical history and allergy tests alone may lead some infants to be labeled with a peanut allergy when they can actually tolerate the food.

Sources indicate that among the infants who reacted during the challenges, 61 experienced anaphylaxis, a severe allergic reaction that can affect breathing and blood pressure. This represented 12% of infants with a positive challenge and 7.8% of all infants who underwent testing. Medical teams safely managed these severe allergic reactions.

Researchers also found that infants who reacted to peanut generally had higher skin prick test results and Ara h 2-specific IgE levels than those who did not react.

However, these test results did not reliably indicate how much peanut would trigger a reaction or how severe that reaction would be.

Of the 394 infants who began peanut oral immunotherapy, 384 (97.5%) successfully started treatment at a dose below the amount that had triggered a reaction during their food challenge.

The researchers say these findings support considering supervised oral food challenges to confirm suspected peanut allergies before starting treatment or recommending long-term avoidance.

Erin Banta, MD, a board certified allergist and immunologist who treats both children and adults at Latitude Food Allergy Care in Great Neck, New York, remarked these findings are significant because they provide evidence for early use of oral food challenges in infants with peanut reactions.

“In those with mild-moderate prior reactions to peanut, early oral food challenge may allow for either delabeling of food allergy (in 1/3 of the patients in this study) or diagnosis of food allergy,” she told Healthline.

Banta, who wasn’t involved in the study, added that early delabeling takes a significant burden off the patient and their family.

“On the other hand,” she explained, “early diagnosis allows for early initiation of treatment with oral immunotherapy at a time in the patient’s life associated with the greatest success rates.”.

Banta further noted that the study offers different pathways for oral immunotherapy based on the patient’s reaction threshold. This means that some patients may be able to complete treatment more quickly due to their individual threshold dose.

Lindsey Forstie, FNP, a family nurse practitioner with clinical training and experience in allergy and asthma care at Carefree Allergy in Phoenix, AZ, added that while further evaluation may be needed to confirm a peanut allergy diagnosis, it’s vital for parents not to try introducing peanuts at home.

“Instead, they should speak with their pediatrician or allergist about appropriate testing and whether a supervised food challenge is safe and necessary,” she noted.

According to Forstie, who was also not part of the study, the goal is to avoid unnecessary food restrictions while also keeping children safe.

“The key message is that not every positive allergy test means a child has a food allergy,” she told Healthline. “Accurate diagnosis helps protect children while allowing those who are not allergic to enjoy a more normal, less restrictive diet.”.

  • According to recent reports, roughly 70 iX5 electric SUVs are rolling off the assembly line every day, alongside gas, diesel, and hybrid-powered models.
  • 2027 BMW iX5 production in Spartanburg, South Carolina.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the first American-made electric BMW is now being assembled at the company’s plant in Spartanburg, South Carolina. It’s a significant moment for the German automaker in the U.S., but it’s just the beginning of a much larger strategy, which will include no fewer than six U.S.-built EVs by the end of the decade.

According to recent reports, roughly 70 iX5 electric SUVs are rolling off the assembly line every day, alongside gas, diesel, and hybrid-powered models. All X5 powertrain versions are based on the same architecture, enabling the car manufacturer to share the same assembly line for multiple fuel types.

2027 BMW iX5 production in Spartanburg, South Carolina.

Initially, BMW’s goal was to build no fewer than 100,000 iX5s in 2027 in Spartanburg, but that target has reportedly been revised to 60,000, according to Automotive News. The automaker has not provided production volume estimates for the iX5, but a tech giant representative remarked that roughly one in four X5s will be electric for the near future.

Sources indicate that “Currently, the market is looking like 20-25 percent EVs for the immediate three months,” said Kavit Antani, general manager of vehicle assembly. “As the market sees these vehicles come through, it might shift.”.

Suppliers have reportedly been given a target of 175,000 EVs in 2028 and 2029, but that’s still a long way from now, and judging from what has happened in the American electric car market in the previous two years, the target could shift significantly.

The batteries that power the newly introduced iX5 come from a new plant 15 miles away in Woodruff, where the first mass-produced packs started their journey to Spartanburg to be fitted to finished chassis earlier this week.

In a recent development, the first Gen6 cylindrical cells used in completed packs will be sourced from AESC in China, BMW confirmed for Automotive News, but the German automaker will switch suppliers toward the end of the decade. LG Energy Solution will supply the car manufacturer’s facilities in the U.S. with locally made cells, while Samsung SDI will supply European factories.

It has been revealed that BMW is not backing down from its strategy to build six EVs in America by 2030. The iX5 is the first, and it will likely be followed by the iX7, iX6, and a performance-oriented iX5 M, according to BMW Blog.

According to recent reports, the 2027 BMW iX5 is powered by a 144-kilowatt-hour battery that can be recharged from 10% to 80% in 22 minutes. Its estimated range sits at an impressive 450 miles, while its dual-motor powertrain delivers 570 horsepower and 594 pound-feet of torque. Pricing starts at $79,800.

West Coast Customs turns a Tesla Model 3 into a 1955 Chevy Bel Air

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1098 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Coast Customs has finished its first electric Chevy Bel Air, and there’s not much Chevy left under the paint.
  • The result, called Project B-Zero, looks like a ’55 Chevy from the curb and like a Model 3 as soon as you open the door.
  • It has been revealed that in the shop’s newly introduced video, “The First Ever Electric Bel Air,” founder and CEO Ryan Friedlinghaus explains that a longtime client, Troy Swope, wants to convert an entire car collection to electric and picked the Bel Air to go first.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Coast Customs has finished its first electric Chevy Bel Air, and there’s not much Chevy left under the paint. The Burbank shop cut the body off a Tesla Model 3, kept the entire rolling platform, and set a 1955 Bel Air shell on top of it.

The result, called Project B-Zero, looks like a ’55 Chevy from the curb and like a Model 3 as soon as you open the door. And it charges at Tesla Superchargers.

It has been revealed that in the shop’s newly introduced video, “The First Ever Electric Bel Air,” founder and CEO Ryan Friedlinghaus explains that a longtime client, Troy Swope, wants to convert an entire car collection to electric and picked the Bel Air to go first. WCC had previously built the same client a Chevelle with a massive gas engine.

Friedlinghaus, who drives a Tesla himself, decided against pulling the Model 3’s motors and battery out and fitting them into the old Chevy. Instead, the Tesla stays whole and the Chevy becomes the body kit.

That’s a formula WCC has used for years with gas cars. The shop calls it “old school meets fresh school”: an old GTO body on a new GTO, an old Camaro on a new Camaro, an old Mustang on a new Mustang. B-Zero is the first time it did it with a Tesla underneath.

“It sounds easy, but that process was tedious,” Friedlinghaus noted.

It has been revealed that before any Chevy sheet metal went on, the crew took the bare Model 3 skateboard for a spin on the streets around the shop, with no doors, no lights and no seatbelts. Friedlinghaus joked about how many safety violations they were racking up. But it drove fine.

According to recent reports, the real headache was the wheelbase. A 1955 Chevy rides on a 115-inch wheelbase, while the Model 3 sits at 113.2 inches. On its gas builds, WCC can cut, shorten or lengthen the newer car’s frame to match the old body. You can’t do that with a Tesla, since the floor is the battery pack.

So the shop changed the body instead, stretching the Bel Air’s rear wheel wells so the wheels sit where they look like they belong.

The client wanted the exterior to read as a mostly stock Bel Air. The original car was red, so WCC kept it red, with a satin finish and gloss black accents.

Industry observers note that inside, it’s a Model 3. The shop kept the Tesla’s interior, including the steering wheel and center touchscreen, and modified it to fit the Chevy body. The seats got black suede with white stitching in an octagon pattern that Friedlinghaus said was borrowed from the Lamborghini Urus, plus red accents and a “B-Zero” script on the dash.

Friedlinghaus noted the goal was for people to see “a really nice Bel Air” from the outside, then open the door and find a Tesla. He also expects some double takes when it pulls into a Supercharger station.

In a recent development, he admits the reaction has been split. Plenty of people are mad that the shop electrified a Bel Air, and plenty of others think it came out great. The client is clearly in the second camp, describing the car as easy to drive and saying every trip in it feels like an event.

Here’s the full build video from West Coast Customs:.

This is sick. I know Tesla doesn’t care about personal car ownership anymore, but they should really sell their platform so shops can do these conversions without using salvage vehicles.

Well I was really interested in this build until I read how they kept it entirely Tesla inside. Not at all what I was thinking or what I'd call a true old car conversion to EV. Instead, they simply transformed the outside of a Tesla into an old looking car. To me, even the outside looks too far removed from the original Bel Air and more like a street rod. If that's what the owner wants and paid for, great.

According to recent reports, but for me, I would never do a conversion like that. I really want to convert an older 70's or 80's or early 90's Cadillac into an EV. But for me, I will insist that the outside and inside look 100% like the original car with just an EV powertrain.

Don’t get me wrong, if you can recycle a salvage, that’s good, but it can’t always be done.

According to recent reports, compare it to the 1966 Mustang that a Sacramento Tesla parts shop converted earlier this year. That project took about $40,000 and two years, with the team grafting sections of a Model 3 floor into the Mustang. It’s an amazing build, but it’s a lot of custom engineering. WCC’s approach skips most of that. You keep Tesla’s crash structure, battery thermal management, software, over-the-air updates and Supercharger access, because you never took the car apart in the first place. It’s closer to what S-Klub did with its Model 3-based Mercedes 300SL than a traditional drivetrain swap.

In a recent development, the purists will hate it. That’s fine. This Bel Air will get driven more in a year than most restored ones get driven in a decade.

Latest Update: Lamborghini Temerario Spyder Delivers Open-Air Access to Its 10,000-RPM V-8

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (711 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Roadandtrack

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Lamborghini has its product development schedule finely tuned.
  • Recent findings suggest that formally introduced Thursday morning at the Academy Museum or Motion Pictures in Los Angeles, the Temerario Spyder isn’t surprising, but it’s still stunning.
  • The folding solid top itself was co-developed by Germany’s Webasto, the venerable firm that’s also behind folding top modules from the Mazda MX-5 Miata RF to the Ferrari California.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lamborghini has its product development schedule finely tuned. Of course, there was a convertible version of the Temerario coming. And on Wednesday, November 18, the automaker unveiled it for the first time—and it is called, of course, the Temerario Spyder.

Recent findings suggest that formally introduced Thursday morning at the Academy Museum or Motion Pictures in Los Angeles, the Temerario Spyder isn’t surprising, but it’s still stunning. The Temerario was designed with the Spyder always in mind; as such, there’s space enough behind the two seats for the new power folding hardtop to snick down inside almost perfectly vertically. The firewall between the cockpit and the mid-mounted, twin-turbocharged V-8 doesn’t change its location, but the space behind the seats is utilized differently.

The folding solid top itself was co-developed by Germany’s Webasto, the venerable firm that’s also behind folding top modules from the Mazda MX-5 Miata RF to the Ferrari California. This is the first Lambo to use a retractable hardtop.

10 electric actuators split the two-piece top, open a hatch behind the seats, and move the structure down into its narrow warren. It’s a fully electric system, so there are no hydraulic lines to split open. Lamborghini says the power top adds about 100 kilograms (220 pounds) to the Temerario’s mass, but that’s all at the center of the car, so that front-to-rear weight balance is maintained. With the roof open, says the maker, the center of gravity drops about three millimeters from where it is when closed.

The hardtop should also produce close to a coupe-like experience when it is closed.“We reinforce the structure of the Spyder,” explains Fermin Soneira, Lambo’s chief technical officer, about the Temerario Spyder’s aluminum space frame. “So, for example, we use some hydroformed pieces in place of castings at some points.”.

The Temerario Spyder takes the market position that was once held by the Huracan Spyder, and Lamborghini claims this new architecture is six percent stiffer in torsional rigidity and nine percent up in dynamic bending stiffness than that car. If all that stiff isn’t stiffy enough, there’s also a six percent increase in dynamic torsional rigidity. So, it’s a super-stiffy thing.

Industry observers note that the increase in weight means the suspension has been slightly tweaked to deal with it. “If you change the weight, you have to change the spring rate to keep the same natural frequency,” says Soneira. “In this case, it was not about leaving everything the same, but also about increasing comfort in the ‘Strada’ drive mode. Still, if you go to the Hockenheimring, there’s less than a one second per lap difference between the coupe and the Spyder.”.

Top up or down, the most spectacular element of every Temerario is the flat-plane crank, 4.0-liter twin-turbo V-8 that’s incorporated into the hybrid all-wheel drive powertrain. With a lightweight reciprocating assembly that includes titanium connecting rods, the engine will spin to a thrilling 10,000-rpm redline. “We have a new calibration of the engine sound,” adds Soneira, “so you end up with a slightly different voice than in the coupe. The target is always ‘let’s keep improving,’ so these changes will come to the coupe too.”.

Combined with three electric motors, the Temerario has 907 horsepower aboard—and despite all the electronic hickey-doos, it still stirs up and blasts like a true supercar. That’s not likely to change with the Spyder.

In a recent development, production of the Spyder will be done in batches along the regular Temerario assembly line, with the first saleable models due to be completed as this is published. Lamborghini expects about 50 percent of Temerario production to be Spyders. Prices haven’t been announced, but should start around $400,000 and go up from there only limited by the buyer’s imagination and wallet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, heartopia, the new cosy life sim from XD Games, has officially arrived on mobile, right on schedule. If you’ve been keeping up with Heartopia news, you’re likely already aware that the game has pushed back its Steam release to an indeterminate point in 2026.

Doesn’t look like it mattered much, however, as this has already been a major launch on iOS and Android — it probably helps that PC players aren't being entirely left out of the fun, since the game is already available there via XD's own cross-device platform TapTap.

XD Games announced today that Heartopia has reached the top spot on the App Store’s downloads page for free games, and it managed to do so in more than 50 countries and regions worldwide.

It has been revealed that the developer is celebratig by offering players a lot of free stuff. If you're feeling lucky, you’ll find new outfits and furniture in three gacha banners (Gilded Acorn Exhibitions): Polar Hymn, The Frostguard, and Coolplayism.

It has been revealed that XD Games states you can expect regular updates to add more content, through Fashionwaves and Festivals. In fact, the first season - Winter Frost - is already penciled in for sometime in late January, and it’s going to add appropriately wintery activities like ice skating and snowman-building.

In February, a My Little Pony collaboration event will kick off, bringing latest inspired outfits, and vehicles to the game.

Latest Update: Egg Donation: Is It Private, or a Secret?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1116 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 19, 2026 | Reviewed by Jessica Schrader.
  • When it comes to donor conception, there is an important difference between protecting your privacy and keeping a secret.
  • A woman I was working with recently voiced that her biggest concern about using an egg donor was disclosure.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 19, 2026 | Reviewed by Jessica Schrader.

When it comes to donor conception, there is an important difference between protecting your privacy and keeping a secret.

A woman I was working with recently voiced that her biggest concern about using an egg donor was disclosure. She worried about how certain family members might react. She anticipated judgment, unwanted opinions, and criticism.

In a recent development, she wasn't questioning whether egg donation was right for her. Rather, she was questioning who needed to know and whether that knowledge could come back to hurt her or her family.

Recent findings suggest that our work raised two important questions: Whose information is it to share? And what is the difference between privacy and secrecy?

These terms are often used interchangeably, but privacy and secrecy are not necessarily the same thing.

Privacy is about choosing what information to share, with whom and when. Secrecy, on the other hand, often involves deliberately withholding information, sometimes because of shame, fear, or anticipated judgment.

According to recent reports, take, for example, a woman who decides not to tell her mother-in-law that she used an egg donor. Perhaps their relationship is difficult. Perhaps she knows her mother-in-law has strong opinions about what makes a family.

It has been revealed that naturally, she may worry that her child will be treated or seen differently. And alongside this may be a concern that her own place as a mother will somehow be questioned.

In a recent development, does that mean she is keeping a secret? Perhaps. But it may also be about privacy. She may simply be sparing herself from a conversation she doesn't want or need to have. This is personal information that belongs to her, her partner and their child. It is not necessarily something the wider family needs to know.

But she may also feel that she has no choice but to hide the information because she fears how her mother-in-law might react.

This is where privacy and secrecy can overlap. She may want to keep the information private, while also feeling that she cannot safely share it. Both can be true at the same time.

And keeping something secret does not automatically mean that someone feels ashamed or that their decision is wrong.

Recent findings suggest that while parents have every right to decide who knows about their fertility treatment, donor conception also involves another person: the child. And the child's relationship with this information is different. For the child, it is part of the story of how they came into the world.

It has been revealed that research supports telling donor-conceived children about their origins early, using age-appropriate language and making it part of their developing understanding of themselves, rather than a “one and done” significant conversation when the child is older (Ilioi et al., 2017; Duff & Goedeke, 2024). There can be something deeply reassuring about growing up with this knowledge, rather than having to make sense of it for the first time later in life.

As the child grows, the conversation also grows. Questions change, new feelings emerge, and things that seemed unimportant at five may take on a different meaning at fifteen.

But what happens when parents tell their child about their conception and then ask them not to tell anyone else?

In a recent development, parents may have understandable reasons for wanting to keep donor conception within the immediate family. They may want to protect their child from judgment, insensitive comments, or rejection.

But imagine a child who has always known they were conceived through egg donation, yet has been told not to mention it to grandparents or friends.

Sources indicate that perhaps a friend asks why they don't look like their mother. The child may want to explain but hesitate, remembering that their parents don't want anyone to know. In this way they are caught between wanting to talk about themselves and worrying about upsetting their parents.

A child may also begin to wonder: Why can we talk about this at home but not outside? Is there something wrong with how I was conceived? This is where privacy may begin to feel like secrecy. Privacy gives a child a choice about what they share, while secrecy may leave them feeling responsible for keeping something hidden.

Industry observers note that as children grow older, they develop their own feelings about their genetic origins. Some may want to talk openly about being donor-conceived, others may prefer privacy. What matters is that the child is gradually given the language, understanding and freedom to decide what they feel comfortable sharing.

For example, they might say, “My parents needed help from an egg donor to have me.”.

Or equally, “I don't really want to talk about that.”.

Recent findings suggest that both are reasonable responses. The important difference is that the choice belongs to them.

It has been revealed that it is OK for parents and children to have different feelings about disclosure. What is vital is that parents recognize their own anxieties and try not to pass them on to their child. The child should feel free to develop their own feelings about their origins, without carrying the weight of their parents' worries.

This can be a complex challenge for parents to come to terms with. And it doesn't have to be neatly resolved. It can just be.

Not everyone will understand or approve. Some may have deeply held beliefs about genetics and family relationships. Others may ask intrusive questions or make insensitive comments. You cannot necessarily prevent those reactions, but you can decide how much access those individuals have to your private lives.

In a recent development, depending on your family and community, it may also be important to prepare your child for the fact that people have different ideas about what makes a family. Not everyone will agree with your views, and they don't have to. This too is part of diversity. There are many different ways to be human.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ionna, the electric vehicle charging consortium backed by major U.S.
  • In just over two years after the company was founded, it already has 224 operational sites across dozens of states.
  • It has been revealed that the organization on Wednesday opened its largest and fanciest charging location in the U.S., in Westminster, California.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ionna, the electric vehicle charging consortium backed by major U.S. automakers including General Motors and Toyota, is growing its footprint in the U.S. at an astonishing pace.

In just over two years after the company was founded, it already has 224 operational sites across dozens of states. Now, it’s announcing a latest flagship location, better access for the growing pool of Tesla drivers, more powerful stations, and discounted charging rates for Jeep, Dodge, and Fiat EV drivers.

It has been revealed that the organization on Wednesday opened its largest and fanciest charging location in the U.S., in Westminster, California. The new Rechargery has 22 stalls and is full of amenities.

According to recent reports, it has canopies over the charging bays, outdoor seating, and a dedicated driver lounge. That's not it. You also get an arcade machine and round the clock access to Wi-Fi, coffee machine, and restrooms.

Seth Cutler, the CEO of Ionna, told InsideEVs in an interview that the organization partnered with Amazon to build a 900-square-foot convenience store at the location which features the e-commerce giant’s Just Walk Out technology.

It lets customers tap their card while entering and directly walk out after shopping without having to stand in line or physically pay through a payment terminal.

“We're moving really fast to build this network up and provide a differentiated experience for customers,” Cutler said.

He added that multiple EVs can simultaneously charge at their maximum speeds at this station. Because it is backed by a whopping 4 megawatts of grid power, there are practically no power constraints for every day EV drivers.

Industry observers note that “You could have 10 Lucid Gravitys and they can all pull 400 kilowatts,” Cutler mentioned. “There’s only load management at the charger level,” he added.

That charger-level limit comes from how the hardware is set up. Each Ionna charging tower can deliver up to 400 kW, and each tower has two cables serving two parking spots.

If only one car is plugged in, the charger can dispense the full 400 kW, as long as the car can accept that speed. If two cars are plugged into the same tower, they share that 400 kW between them. The towers don’t draw from each other, so one busy tower never slows down the one next to it.

Recent findings suggest that that means drivers can get back swiftly on the road and the chance of long queues building up are less. In other words, you spend more time driving and less time charging.

The organization is also preparing for future EVs that push the boundaries of ultra-fast charging speeds, at least for non-Chinese automakers.

Cutler said groundwork had already started to build 500-kilowatt stations in the U.S. Its current network comprises 400 kW-capable Alpitronic Hyperchargers, which are plenty quick by their own right.

He didn’t say when and where exactly these fresh chargers will open, but he added that the probable timeline is 2028 when more EVs on the market will actually be able to benefit from such high charging speeds.

Only a handful of EVs in the U.S. can currently accept even 400 kilowatts, let alone 500 kW. The Lucid Gravity, Porsche Cayenne Electric, and the BMW iX3 are capable of accepting 400 kW.

The upcoming Mercedes AMG GT will be able to charge at 600 kW when deliveries start next year. Owners have reported the Tesla Cybertruck pulling 500 kW for a brief window at the newer V4 Superchargers capable of dispensing such speeds.

Recent findings suggest that that noted, Tesla drivers can now get auto charge at Ionna stations using fleet charging organization Presto's app. Plug & Charge is already enabled at Ionna for BMW, General Motors, Toyota, Volvo, Rivian, Ford, Hyundai, Kia, Mercedes-Benz, Porsche, and Volvo.

Downloading another smartphone app, however, might be unnecessary for Tesla drivers who already use the ubiquitous Supercharger network.

Starting in December, Ionna is also offering a 10% discount for EVs under the Stellantis umbrella. So drivers with the Jeep Wagoneer S, Dodge Charger Daytona, and the Fiat 500e will benefit from lower charging rates. If they have a connected services subscription, they get an additional 15% discount at Ionna taking the total to 25%.

And finally, Ionna’s network is now dense enough for coast-to-coast road trips just using Ionna charging stations. That’s something the company demonstrated this week with multiple drivers that set-off from Fresh York, Raleigh, and Miami among other cities in a journey that culminated in California.

It’s a big achievement that proves that even though EV sales are up and down, the country’s charging network is growing quickly and is now better than ever.

In a recent development, and unfortunately, this isn’t entirely surprising. We’ve already reported on some strange battery behavior with the newly introduced e-bikes, as well as customers having to send their bikes back for repairs.

In a message sent to customers, ALSO explained that it was pausing shipments to address several software problems before more bikes reach riders.

“We’ve identified a few software-based challenges, such as charging behavior, that are impacting some bikes,” the manufacturer explained.

ALSO notes its engineers are working on a firmware revision to resolve the problems, with shipments expected to resume in approximately two weeks.

The pause affects the remaining Launch Edition deliveries as well as the beginning of Performance Edition shipments, both of which will now arrive later than previously promised.

The announcement follows earlier reports of unusual charging and discharging behavior on the TM-B, which we previously highlighted as some of the growing pains facing Rivian’s ambitious upcoming e-bike venture.

We’ve also reported on customers needing to return their bikes for repairs, raising questions about how smoothly the tech giant’s initial rollout was progressing.

The issues align with many of our initial concerns we discussed a year ago when the bike was first unveiled, namely that the high-tech design means the bike incorporates many fresh and proprietary systems that could each lead to complicated and costly failures.

Now ALSO has officially acknowledged software problems affecting some bikes, including charging behavior, though it hasn’t detailed the full extent of the complications or confirmed whether they are directly related to those earlier reports.

The bike represents a fairly radical departure from traditional electric bicycles, with proprietary technology throughout its drivetrain and control systems. That makes software an especially crucial part of the ownership experience.

Industry observers note that to ALSO’s credit, pausing deliveries to fix known problems is probably the right move. Nobody wants to receive a premium-priced electric bicycle only to discover that it needs an immediate trip back to the manufacturer.

But for customers who have already waited longer than expected, another delay is undoubtedly frustrating.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that becky the basset hound is giving new meaning to the term “man’s best friend.” On November 12, she walked to the Whiteface Lodge, a ski resort in Lake Placid, New York. The hotel staff immediately recognized the dog, but not because of her sparkling personality or floppy ears. Becky’s owner has dementia, and the unnamed man has disappeared before.

The team at Whiteface called the New York State Police (NYSP), who contacted the Department of Conservation (DEC) Forest Rangers for assistance with the search. Four NYSP officers and 14 Rangers used drones and another dog (a bloodhound) to search for the missing person. According to Charlie Foutch, the lead Ranger on the search, it was about 25 to 30 degrees Fahrenheit overnight.

According to recent reports, at 10 a.m. the next morning, a hunter who was searching just ahead of the group heard someone fall and scream. He found the missing man off to the side of a trail in a draining area with open woods. Ranger Sabo arrived on the scene shortly after. The 69-year-old man was not wearing gloves or shoes, and was suffering from some frostbite on his feet and hands. He was still alert and talking.

“We’re always looking for live people. That’s our goal is to find a live person,” said Fouch. “And a lot of people are really tough. This gentleman didn’t have shoes on when we found him in the morning or mittens or gloves, so he had been out there for some period of time at night. And he still did okay. Sometimes if you keep moving in that situation, you generate enough heat to do okay.”.

Due to his injuries and the location off the trail, a hoist was the safest and quickest way to get him to safety. Ranger Martin used a cable to hoist him up to a helicopter, while NYSP Pilot Engle flew them to the hospital.

In addition to this coordination between hunters, the NYSP, and DEC, Fouch noted that Becky the basset hound made this happy ending possible.

“I think if the dog had not shown up at Whiteface, that gentleman definitely would have had a different outcome,” stated Fouch. “It definitely would have been much harder to find him. He may not have survived the rest of the day and probably not another night. The dog definitely contributed to him being saved so rapidly.”.
